lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Replace the example URL and contact details if they are placeholders.
Make sure the link leads directly to work you want a reviewer to see.
Remove the date of birth and nationality from a US-focused resume unless requested.
items.because: They are generally not needed for screening.

items.says: Check that “Expected Jun 2026” is still accurate when you apply.
Replace “Country” if it is a placeholder.
Use consistent location formatting across schools and jobs.
Define whether the 35% accuracy gain is relative or in percentage points.
items.because: Otherwise, the result is hard to judge.

items.says: Briefly identify the evaluation set for the accuracy result.
items.because: Otherwise, the result is hard to judge.

items.says: Clarify what “reviewer disagreement” measures and what was counted.
items.because: Readers need to understand the 14%-to-6% change.

items.says: Explain why restricting signals improved reviewer disagreement.
Clarify whether the tool-call and latency reductions came from the same evaluation.
Expand or contextualize GRPO if the target audience may not know it.
Use a spelling convention consistent with the rest of the resume for “penalises.”
items.because: It differs from the otherwise US-oriented presentation.

items.says: Specify what “citation quality” means if citations matter to the role.
The assistant-only loss-masking bullet repeats the first bullet.
items.because: It does not describe a distinct contribution.

items.says: Assistant-only loss masking does not by itself explain more faithful reproduction of tool outputs.
items.because: The bullet should state only behavior the evaluation established.

items.says: Clarify whether the backlog drop can reasonably be attributed to the triage branch.
Clarify the period or baseline against which the backlog was measured.
Clarify whether “4x” means memory fell to one-quarter of its original use.
Say whether the precision change affected model quality or training throughput.
Check whether the build-failing load test represents the reported p95 conditions.
items.because: Otherwise, distinguish the test threshold from production latency.

items.says: Change “adds” to past tense.
items.because: It does not match the role and other bullets.

items.says: Explain what the three-day release cycle is compared with.
Quantify the backlog or dispatch improvement if possible.
items.because: The bullet says only that delays were removed.

items.says: Substantiate or remove the adoption claim with a specific action and observed result.
items.because: “AI-first engineering practices,” “accelerating delivery,” and “improving outcomes” are too broad.

items.says: Explain what remained under 10K tokens.
Explain how useful context was preserved.
items.because: Size alone does not establish quality.

items.says: Check that “grew 100x” has a meaningful starting point.
Clarify whether the deadlocks and lost results were observed in tests or production.
Explain what “50-way fan-out” refers to.
Identify the most important metrics or the decisions they enabled.
Specify what was ranked for the Kendall correlation.
items.because: That makes the validation claim easier to assess.

items.says: Clarify whether the 400+ trials were independent reports or variants.
items.because: That makes the validation claim easier to assess.

items.says: The backlog bullet duplicates the Mobility Systems result.
The backlog result appears unrelated to the Research-Agent Evaluation Framework project.
